'''Janet Irene Sprent''', [[Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] (born 1934) is a British [[Botany|botanical]] scientist, and [[emeritus professor]] at [[University of Dundee|the University of Dundee]].<ref name=lifesci>{{cite web|url=http://www.lifesci.dundee.ac.uk/people/janet-sprent|title=Professor Janet Sprent OBE, FRSE|accessdate=1 May 2015| work = Dundee University}}</ref>

==Education and career==
After graduating from [[Imperial College London]] in 1954 with a [[BSc]] and [[Associate of the Royal College of Science|ARCS]],<ref name=Profile>{{citation
  | title = Profile: Janet I. Sprent
  | work = New Phytologist
  | year = 2017
  | volume = 215
  | pages = 38–39
  | doi  = 10.1111/nph.14618| doi-access = free
  }}</ref> Sprent worked for a year at [[Rothamsted Research|Rothamsted Experimental Station]] before undertaking a [[PhD]] at the [[University of Tasmania]]. She taught [[botany]] for two years at [[Rochester Grammar School]] before being awarded a lectureship at [[Goldsmiths, University of London|Goldsmiths College]] in 1960.<ref name=Profile/> Sprent moved to [[Dundee]], [[Scotland]], in 1967, where she secured a research fellowship at the [[University of Dundee]]. She became dean of the Faculty of Science and Engineering in 1987, and was awarded a personal chair in 1989. She also served as the Head of the Department of [[Biological Sciences]] from 1992 to 1995. Eventually, she became the deputy principal of Dundee University from 1995 until her retirement in 1998.

==Research areas==
Sprent's primary research interests lie in the field of [[nitrogen fixation]] in [[legumes]]. Sprent would bring her works with across multiple different countries as she continued to research legume taxonomy and how they have evolved through processes such as [[Root nodule|nodulation.]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gallery of Leguminologists  - Legume Data Portal |url=https://www.legumedata.org/beanbag/70/issue-70-gallery-leguminologists |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=www.legumedata.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
In recognition of the contribution she has made to the understanding of nitrogen fixation in legume symbioses, Sprent was awarded a [[Doctor of Science]] degree by the [[University of London]]  in 1988. Then, in 2006, an honorary Doctor of Agriculture from the [[Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences]].<ref name=Profile/> She was inducted as a [[Royal Society of Edinburgh|Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1990 and awarded an [[OBE]] in 1996.<ref name=lifesci /><ref>{{citation
  | title = Professor Janet Sprent
  | work = The Royal Society of Edinburgh
  | url = https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/professor-janet-sprent/
  | accessdate = 21 February 2023}}</ref> In 2013, the nitrogen-fixing bacterium ''[[Burkholderia sprentiae]]'' (later renamed ''Paraburkholderia sprentiae'') was named after her.<ref name=lifesci /><ref>{{citation

  | volume = 63

  | doi = 10.1099/ijs.0.048777-0}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
